clue.text: Reportedly remained sober

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word for remained is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have stayed off the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A staid person is serious and restrained, which is one sense of sober.

clue.text: Cut leave dropping week

indicators.note: in a down entry, dropping says the letter for week falls further down the word

parts.note: to swan off is to leave casually

explanation.surface: A worker trims a holiday by giving up a week of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves the W of SWAN OFF down one place, giving SAWN-OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn-off describes something shortened by sawing, as in a sawn-off shotgun, so it means cut short.

clue.text: Advanced group for skilful person, …

parts.note: a department, DEPT for short, is a group within an organisation

explanation.surface: An advanced set is picked out for one talented individual, the thought running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is an expert, someone highly skilled at something.

clue.text: … one repeatedly coming back from Canadian adventures

indicators.note: coming back means the letters found are read in reverse order
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow
repeatedly points out that the run of letters appears twice in a row across these two words

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, an expert keeps returning from trips in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 2 down: 'one' means one skilful person. NAD sits in caNADian and again across caNADventures, hence 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo and karate a dan is a black-belt grade, and so also a person holding one, an expert.

clue.text: Copper's covering evidence

parts.note: a copper is a penny coin, P; the 's means has
a roof is a covering over a building

explanation.surface: A police officer is hiding the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is a penny coin, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is the evidence that establishes a fact.

clue.text: Dog handler's first old expression of disgust

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: handler's first means the opening letter of the word handler's

explanation.surface: A dog handler's original exclamation was one of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugh is an old spelling of pooh or pah, an exclamation of contempt or disgust.

clue.text: Voluntary work supported by revolutionary Latino

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters of Latino are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unpaid work backed by a Latin American revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns LATINO into TIONAL, which goes under OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to choice, not compulsory, so it is voluntary.

clue.text: After change of heart congregation gets criticism

indicators.note: a change of heart here means the middle letter of the word for congregation is swapped for another

parts.note: a vicar's congregation is his flock

explanation.surface: After a priest has a change of heart, the parishioners turn on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the central O of FLOCK for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Flack is informal for harsh criticism, as in taking flack, a variant of flak.

clue.text: Pat's logo designed for sports fixture

indicators.note: designed means the letters of the phrase are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A man named Pat created the emblem for a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports fixture' suggests a match, but here a fixture is a fixed object on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalpost is one of the uprights fixed on a football or rugby pitch.

clue.text: The Spanish and British propose to return gardening tool

indicators.note: to return means the combined letters are read going back the other way

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
to bid is to propose or offer

explanation.surface: A Spaniard and a Briton plan to bring back a garden implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dibble is a pointed hand implement gardeners use to make holes for seedlings and bulbs.

clue.text: Time to greet prince going with crusader?

indicators.note: going means a letter leaves the word for to greet

parts.note: in Scots, to greet is to weep
the crusaders included knights, so a crusader is one example of a knight; hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Is it time to welcome a prince travelling with a medieval warrior?
explanation.walkthrough: 'greet' looks like welcoming, but it is the Scottish word for weep; WEEP loses P to give WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is an evening from Monday to Friday, a period of time.

clue.text: Trouble with one consuming old mayonnaise

indicators.note: consuming means the letters swallow another piece whole

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: There is a problem with somebody eating stale mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic-flavoured version of mayonnaise from Provence.

clue.text: Slow-witted Hobbits regularly ignored exercise

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of the word is dropped, keeping the rest

parts.note: to exercise a power is to use it

explanation.surface: Dim hobbits often skip their workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse describes someone dull or slow to understand.

clue.text: Saturate too much

definitions.meaning: to soak something thoroughly in liquid, as tea leaves in water
an informal sense of excessive, said of a price that is unreasonably high

explanation.definitionFit: Steep means both to soak in liquid and, of a price or demand, excessive.

clue.text: Society priest maybe pursuing Esther?

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Bible; the question mark marks it as one example
a priest is a small club used by anglers to kill fish, so it is one kind of club

explanation.surface: A clergyman chases after a woman named Esther.
explanation.walkthrough: 'priest' looks like a clergyman, but it is an angler's small cudgel, a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A book club is a society whose members read and discuss books.

clue.text: Old chess player dumps Charlie for Rod

definitions.note: a rod can mean a person who fishes with one, an angler

indicators.note: dumps means a letter is thrown out of the name

parts.note: Bobby Fischer was the American world chess champion of the 1970s
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A veteran chess player leaves a man named Charlie for another named Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name, but it stands for an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisher is someone who fishes, an angler, who can be called a rod after the tackle.

clue.text: Railway workers put horse in empty sidings

indicators.note: put together with in says one piece is placed inside another
in, with put, says the horse goes within the outer letters
empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: a hunter is a horse bred for fox hunting

explanation.surface: Railwaymen stable a horse in deserted sidings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunters are locomotives, and the staff who work them, moving rolling stock between tracks in railway yards.

clue.text: Aerobic exercises incorporating Latin dance movement

indicators.note: incorporating means taking another piece into the body of the word
exercises suggests putting through moves, so the letters of aerobic are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aerobics routine that includes a Latin dance step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' rearranges AEROBIC to CABRIOE, and 'incorporating' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriole is a ballet leap in which one leg beats against the other in the air.

clue.text: One that may charge money

definitions.meaning: an animal known for charging at whatever threatens it
an old British slang word for cash

explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is famous for charging, and rhino is dated British slang for money.

clue.text: Who nosed about in US social events

indicators.note: about means the letters of the words are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone asks who was snooping around at American parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoedowns are lively gatherings with folk dancing, a rural American tradition.

clue.text: Old children's programme's in top 100

parts.note: to top something is to trump it, to beat it
a ton is a hundred

explanation.surface: A former children's show is in the top hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top 100' looks like a chart, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpton was a 1960s BBC stop-motion children's series about a small town and its fire brigade.

clue.text: Follows lines in recordings

definitions.meaning: to trail or pursue someone by their footprints
the separate bands, or songs, on a record or album

explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow them, and an album's tracks are its individual recorded pieces.

clue.text: Plant working for china maker

parts.note: mint is an aromatic herb plant
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A plant is busy making porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, but it is a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Minton is an English pottery firm, founded in Stoke-on-Trent, famous for its fine porcelain.

clue.text: Where to find tender borders of rosemary

definitions.text: Where to find tender borders of rosemary

parts.note: a tender is one who tends, such as a nurse

indicators.note: borders of means the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A garden centre is where young rosemary plants are raised for borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a nursery raises tender young plants, such as rosemary for borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young plants are raised, and a room for young children cared for by a nurse.

clue.text: A police department charges colonists getting drugs

indicators.note: charges means rushes into, so the police unit goes inside the colonists

parts.note: ants live in colonies
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives arrest settlers found with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colonists' suggests settlers, but it is the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Antacids are medicines that neutralise stomach acid, so they are drugs.

clue.text: Press graduate probing company making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the combined letters are read back to front
probing means pushing into the middle of another piece

parts.note: a PLC is a public limited company
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate investigating a firm that is staging a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' puts MA into PLC to give PMALC, which 'making a comeback' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamp something is to press or grip it tightly.

clue.text: Graphical device left out for craftsperson

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: a plotter is a device that draws graphs and diagrams

explanation.surface: A graphics machine is dropped in favour of an artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter is an artisan who makes pots and ceramics.

clue.text: Men in Romania taking part in summit

indicators.note: taking part in means joining inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the summit is the top
RO is the international vehicle code for Romania

explanation.surface: Romanian delegates attend a summit meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a body of soldiers, and men is a common term for soldiers.

clue.text: Escape with roll of cloth

definitions.meaning: to run off suddenly, as a horse or prisoner does
a length of fabric wound up as it comes from the loom

explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to dash away, and a bolt is a standard roll of woven fabric.

clue.text: In a frenzy over including recipe for curry

indicators.note: including means taking another piece inside
over means turned over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: running amok is being in a frenzy
R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A frantic cook takes in a recipe for a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses AMOK to KOMA, and 'including' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A korma is a mild, creamy Indian curry.

clue.text: Fussy individuals endlessly admitting faults is healthy

indicators.note: admitting means letting another piece in
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an old woman is a fussy, timid person, so fussy individuals can be called women
holes are faults or flaws, as when people pick holes in an argument

explanation.surface: Picky people confessing their failings is good for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fussy individuals' rests on 'old woman', British slang for a fussy, timid person of either sex; 'endlessly' trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome food or activity is good for the body, so healthy.

clue.text: Spike's a penniless western gunfighter

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, so the letter for penny goes

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a lawman and gunfighter of the American West

explanation.surface: A man called Spike is a broke cowboy gunslinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name, but it is a spike of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is the spike of a cereal plant holding the grains, as an ear of corn.

clue.text: State is firmly put in place

definitions.meaning: to assert or put forward as a basis for argument
an older sense meaning to set something in position

explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to lay down a claim as true, and also, more literally, to place or position something.

clue.text: Rough earth found in section of crop yield

indicators.note: found in means the letter goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a section of the letters of crop yield, running from the second letter across the word break, spells ROPY

explanation.surface: Poor soil turns up in part of a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section of' takes ROPY from cROP Yield, and 'found in' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropey is British informal for poor in quality or slightly unwell, so rough.
